summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch printed Tom Allen's denial that he was leaving for England. He blamed Ned Donnelly (George Bruer) and Billy Allen of the Adelphi, and posted a $500 challenge to Joe Coburn.

metadata.notes: no page image; filed as Post-Dispatch but 1876 predates the 1878-12 merger; masthead date not verified

facts.fact: Allen denied he was leaving St. Louis for England, saying he had lived there seven years and intended to stay
facts.quote: Do you think I would go from St. Louis, where I have lived seven years? No; I intend to live in St. Louis.

facts.fact: Allen said Donnelly's real name was George Bruer, a laborer he had trained as a boxer, and that he knocked Donnelly down after Donnelly broke their engagement to go to Chicago
Allen planned to go to Chicago to fill a sparring engagement and return to St. Louis on the 28th
Allen refused to spar with Joe Coburn at Billy Allen's Adelphi Theater, saying Coburn had refused to spar with him in New York
Allen authorized his backer Fred Watkins of 720 Main Street to accept any challenge from Coburn or his friends for $500 a side or more
facts.quote: I have made arrangements with Fred Watkins, my backer, of 720 Main street, to accept any challenge Coburn or his friends may offer for $500 a side or more, and if they mean business, the money will be up in two hours.

facts.fact: Allen said the lease on his Washington Avenue saloon had expired because the building was to be torn down, and his goods were stored at 1222 Collins Street, not sold
facts.quote: The lease on the place I had expired and as they are going to tear down the old house, and re-build of course I had to get out, but I am looking for another place.
